articleTitle: Accurate Nonlinear GaN HEMT Simulations from X- to Ka-Band using a Single ASM-HEMT Model
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents for the first time an investigation of the ASM-HEMT model large-signal accuracy across a wide range of operating frequencies. Comparisons between measured and simulated power sweeps are presented at 10, 20 and 30 GHz. Load-pull measurements and simulations are compared spanning the same frequency range. The large-signal simulations of a single ASM-HEMT model exhibit excellent agreement with all power measurements.

articleTitle: An Origami-Inspired Foldable Reflectarray on a Straight-Major Square-Twist Pattern
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-gain Reflectarray Antenna (RA) design on an origami-inspired foldable structure, which is based on the straight-major square-twist pattern (SMST). The antenna was designed to operate at 16 GHz and direct its main beam along φ = 00, 8 = 300 direction with a gain of 28.34 dBi. The RA was excited by a horn antenna of 14 dBi gain with Q-factor of 5.25 positioned at a distance of 10λ with a 10° offset angle. The foldable nature of our origami-inspired structure provides a 92% packing efficiency of the RA aperture surface area, thereby offering a significant advantage for small satellites and terrestrial tactical applications.

articleTitle: Adaptive Beamforming for mmWave 5G MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: The direction of arrival (DOA) estimation and beamforming are effective methods for spatial diversity realization. Various algorithm already exists for implementing these methods. This paper explore the performance of least mean square algorithm (LMS) beamforming algorithm. This adaptive beamforming algorithm investigates receiver signal processing method that continuously monitor, calculate and update the weights in a continuously changing electromagnetic environment. Several optimization algorithms are studied, and a comparison of the least mean-squared algorithm and the minimum variance distortionless response is investigated with varying parameters (i.e. number of antenna element, element spacing etc.) using analytical method and Matlab simulation. It would be demonstrated through simulation that LMS algorithm increases signal quality by elimination interfering signals and noise by nulling them, while sending maximum signal (beams) to the desired direction.

articleTitle: A Low-Loss 1-4 GHz Optically-Controlled Silicon Plasma Switch
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a low-loss optically-controlled inline RF switch suitable for L- and S-band applications. Under 1.5 W laser power, the switch exhibits a measured ON-state insertion loss of less than 0.33 dB and return loss better than 20 dB across the band. The measured OFF-state isolation ranges from 27 dB at 1 GHz to 17 dB at 4 GHz. The switch comprises a single silicon chiplet excited by a 915-nm laser fiber which creates electron-hole pairs, thereby exciting the ON-state silicon plasma. An optical fiber is guided through the bottom of the RF substrate to illuminate the chiplet, which bridges a 1.075-mm microstrip line gap. To the best of our knowledge, this is the lowest-loss silicon plasma switch demonstrated today.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable and Deployable Miura-Ori RA Analysis for Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A foldable reconfigurable ReflectArray antenna (RA) based on the Miura-Ori origami pattern is presented for CubeSat deep space communications. Designed at 8.425 GHz, the RA is capable of operating with a single beam as well as dual beams. The beamscanning capabilities are a function of the aperture fold θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> and are showcased using a time saving analytical model.

articleTitle: Plasma Switch-Based Technology for High-Speed and High-Power Impedance Tuning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper introduces a new technology for a high-speed, high-power mobile form-factor tuner utilizing gas discharge tube plasma cells as switching components. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first plasma-enabled RF matching network. Technology development is reviewed, the fabrication and measurement of a proof-of-concept switched stub impedance tuner are presented, and techniques for improvement are discussed. The proof-of-concept impedance tuner functions with a 27% bandwidth from 3 to almost 4 GHz and shows a power gain better than -2.5dB across all switching state-frequency combinations at a 50 W input power level with spread coverage of the Smith chart. State change transient timing is measured to be on the order of 500 ns. This technology demonstration highlights the potential of miniaturized, rapidly-tunable, high-power, plasma-based RF devices.

articleTitle: A Synthesis View to Dual-Band Responses With Parallel-Connected Acoustic Wave Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work addresses how to cope with a dual-band filter response through the direct parallel connection of two acoustic wave ladder filters and provides a synthesis view on how to design them individually. Similar to a duplexer, the reflection phase of each filter plays a fundamental role to allow such a connection and, therefore, must be precisely considered at both ports. However, it is not a sufficient condition since, when the filters are connected in parallel, each of them behaves like a source-to-load reactive path on the other. Therefore, their out-of-band rejection suffers a severe degradation if directly connected without any other consideration. This has been observed in a measured filter and this paper provides an explanation of such behaviour. The work also proposes a filter design to overcome such degradation and highlights how filter synthesis can enhance results in a controlled manner.

articleTitle: Dynamically Reconfigurable Direction-Finding Antenna Array for Unmanned Arial Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: One of the more accurate but complex methods of radio direction finding uses the Correlation Methods found in the MUSIC algorithms. Critical to this method is the characterization of the antennas array manifold. The antenna array manifold can be realized in any number of N-antenna elements configured either circularly, or linearly. Once the antenna array is established, the array manifold is characterized where a correlation compares the response to the array manifold to find the best match in order to determine the direction of arrival. Historically, antenna array manifolds are static antenna arrays fixed to the side of aircraft, ships or ground vehicles. In this paper we propose to use of the correlation DF technique using the MUSIC method with a dynamically re-configurable antenna array manifold optimizing the accuracy and improving the frequency response of the direction of arrival. In our application, the benefits of a reconfigurable antenna array outweigh the mechanical complexity of its implementation, and we will first simulate and validate accuracy of the system using the same array at multiple distances and frequencies.

articleTitle: Novel Synthesis Methodology of Lowpass Networks Comprising Generalized Cascaded Trisections
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work presents a novel methodology enabling the synthesis of lowpass networks comprising generalized cascaded trisections (GCTs). The methodology derives the proposed networks from their canonical lowpass counterparts upon the re-synthesis of sub-network blocks in an intuitive fashion. A lowpass filter comprising two GCTs is synthesized. Furthermore, the EM model of a GCT is presented exhibiting performance that is in close agreement with the theory.

articleTitle: Phase Measurement and Correction for Software Defined Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work is motivated by the use of software defined radios (SDRs) to improve the flexibility of, e.g., steerable phased array antennas. While SDRs can be low in cost, they are inherently not phase synchronized, a challenge for the intended application. In this work, a cross correlation method for phase measurement is presented. In simulation, the measured phase never deviated from the actual phase shift by more than 2%, even at an SNR of 0 dB. The approach was further verified via an angle of arrival hardware test at 915 MHz, where the mean phase error between the actual and measurement, over a range of 35°, was less than 1°. The presented SDR phase measurement algorithm provides a simple way to measure and compensate for the initial phase shift in SDRs and can be leveraged for wide variety of phase sensitive SDR applications.

articleTitle: Effects of Electromagnetic Wave Propagations in Large-Signal Analysis of Millimeter-Wave Transistors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A distributed-model-based approach is developed for small- and large-signal analyses of millimeter-wave transistors. To obtain the equivalent circuit model parameters, a structure based extraction technique is utilized. The method employs the physical geometry and structural topology of the device for finding the parameter values based on conformal mapping concepts and incremental inductance rule. The significant contribution of this approach is to incorporate the electromagnetic wave propagation effects in designing the distributed circuit which ensures achieving a universally accurate model over a very broad frequency range. This technique is applied to analyze a GaN MISHEMT device. The simulation results for the gain and output power under the small- and large-signal conditions are obtained for different device widths at various bias points and operating frequencies. To validate the performance of the proposed modeling approach, the results are compared with the measurement.

articleTitle: A Compact Digital Low-IF Dual-PLL Doppler Radar for Remote Vital Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact digital 1ow-IF Doppler radar using two phase-locked loops (PLLs) is proposed to remotely detect vital sign signal of the human subject. The system operates at 2. 41GHz with -6.5dBm transmitting power. By feeding the two PLLs with the same reference signal and configuring them to operate at different frequencies, a l-kHz low- IF signal can be achieved without quadrature mixer involved in the system and the intermediate frequency (IF) signal is directly sampled and processed in the digital domain. Phase coherence of the two PLL output signals has been testified and after that, the vital sign movement of the subject is measured and compared with a pulse oximeter reference. The measured result well agrees with the reference signal at a detection distance of 1.8 m.

articleTitle: Novel Synthesis Methodology of Lowpass Networks Comprising Generalized Cascaded Box Configurations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work presents a novel methodology enabling the synthesis of lowpass networks comprising generalized cascaded box configurations (GCBCs). The methodology derives the proposed networks from their counterparts comprising generalized cascade quadruplets (GCQs) which are essentially derived from their canonical counterparts. A lowpass filter comprising two GCBCs is synthesized and the steps involved are presented demonstrating the design methodology.

articleTitle: Novel Synthesis Methodology of Lowpass Networks Comprising Generalized Cascaded Quadruplets
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work presents a novel methodology enabling the synthesis of lowpass networks comprising generalized cascaded quadruplets (GCQs). The methodology derives the proposed networks from their canonical lowpass counterparts upon the re-synthesis of sub-network blocks in an intuitive fashion. A lowpass filter comprising two GCQs is synthesized and the steps involved are presented demonstrating the design methodology.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Full Duplex Communication for Wireless Network on Chips with OOK Modulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this paper, the inherent advantage of On-Off Keying (OOK) Modulation for full duplex communication has been investigated in the physical layer in the context of short distance on chip communication such as wireless network on chip (WiNoC). Here, the OOK transmitter is designed in a manner such that it also works as an RF canceler. This novel design neither requires an external phase inverter nor an attenuator to achieve the cancellation of the self-interfered signal. The distance between the transmitter and the receiver being very small for WiNoC, the self interference cancellation requirement of the typical 100 dB of power reduces by more than 60%. The isolation achieved by the OOK transmitter cum RF canceler is 19 dB as simulated and shown in this work. This energy efficient OOK transmitter has been designed with BSIM-CMG (Common Multi-Gate) FinFET model at 60 GHz. The power dissipation of the transmitter is 23 mW. In tandem with the path loss in the propagation domain and antenna cross polarization this design meets the required isolation and opens up a great opportunity for using full duplex communication for WiNoCs with the energy efficient non-coherent OOK modulation. No work has investigated the feasibility of full duplex communication for WiNoCs or for any other on-chip communications in the physical layer in the past.

articleTitle: A Fully-Integrated Band-Switchable CMOS Power Amplifier for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work, for the first time, proposes a fully integrated band-switchable RF power amplifier (PA) by using a novel approach towards switching the matching networks. In this approach, two matching networks which can be controlled by digital bits will provide the lower and higher operating frequency bands for the PA. In order to implement the proposed band-switchable PA, a robust RF switch is presented by using resistive body floating technique and 6-terminal triple-well NMOS. The measured results show that the proposed band-switchable power amplifier can operate at 980MHz and 1900MHz as the lower and the higher frequency bands, and delivers saturated output power (Psat) of 21. 3dBm/23.0dBm, output 1-dB compression point (PldB) of 19. 5dBm/21.0dBm, and 3-dB bandwidth of 400MHz/550MHz, respectively, showing promising advancement compared to the state-of-the-art. The proposed power amplifier is designed and implemented in 180nm CMOS process with die area of 3.1mm× 1.6mm.

articleTitle: Entropy Based Exploration in Cognitive Radio Networks using Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Spectrum Access
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper details the practical design of a Cognitive Radio network which uses multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for dynamic spectrum access. Each network node evaluates a neural network model to determine when it can transmit and on what frequency channel. The models are trained offline in simulation to mitigate slow online training time. Furthermore, we propose the use of entropy-based-exploration to dynamically determine when more training is required in the wireless network. Unlike previous work that has only considered similar techniques in theory and simulation, we present over-the-air measurement results for the throughput and channel utilization collected in a large-scale software-defined radio testbed.

articleTitle: Parallelly and Diagonally Placed Meander-Line Slot Resonators for Mutual Coupling Reduction in a 2x2 Patch Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a meander-line (ML) slot resonator inserted on the ground plane to reduce the mutual coupling between closely placed array patches in a 2 x 2 array antenna for 5 GHz WLAN and 3.5 GHz Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS) applications. The distance between the patch elements is 2 mm i.e. $0.033 \lambda_{0}$ for 5 GHz and $0.023 \lambda_{0}$ for 3.5 GHz. The dimension of the ML slot unit cell has been optimized to operate as a band-stop filter at the target frequency. Two types of ML placements are demonstrated: (1) one has the ML slots parallelly placed between the patch elements and (2) the other has the ML slots diagonally placed underneath each patch. Both designs are point symmetric at the center of the 2 x 2 array. More than 55 % area reduction has been achieved compared with conventional 2 x 2 array elements found in literature. A mutual coupling reduction of at least 9 dB has been achieved for all the antenna elements with the diagonal ML slot architecture.

articleTitle: Photonic Curing of mm-Wave Coplanar Waveguides for Conductor Loss Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) techniques for high-frequency electronics have evolved in the past decade to not only offer similar performance as traditional manufacturing, but to offer unprecedented design freedom. One of the main challenges of AM of radio-frequency devices is the losses associated with the printed conductive layers. Recent studies have shown that pulsed laser can enhance the conductivity of the conductive inks. In this work, the photonic curing process, or PulseForgeOR, is applied to AM coplanar waveguides (CPW) to measure its effect on the high-frequency electric conductivity. Dissipative losses are reduced by 2.58 dB, from -4.74dB to -2.16dB, at 40 GHz over a 10 mm long line, after photonic curing, when compared to thermally cured samples.

articleTitle: Miniature K-Band Radar for Agricultural Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Remote sensing for agricultural applications employs multi-spectral data collection. While optical-wavelength normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) is the most common, smart agriculture can benefit from the addition of longer wavelengths to the sensing techniques. A radar operating in the 12.5 cm band (23 to 25 GHz spectrum) is described. The design leverages low-cost commercial ICs and coherent calibration cancellation techniques to sense at standoff distances as short as 10 cm, while providing a small size, weight, and power (SWaP) solution suitable for a variety of platforms. Field trials are overviewed on crops ranging from soybean to grain sorghum validating the ability to measure crop height and structure with high spatial resolution.

articleTitle: High Selectivity Low-Loss Tunable Bandpass Filter with Transmission Zeros Control Using Staircase Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this paper, a new compact staircase resonator is employed to design low-loss and high selectivity varactor-based tunable bandpass filter at 1.58-1.88 GHz on ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 10.2, 1.27 mm Duroid substrate. The proposed tunable staircase filter has a constant 3-dB fractional bandwidth of 10.6±0.5% and low insertion loss <; 2 dB allover the tuning band. Additionally, owing to the resonator's structure, an efficient transmission zeros tuning approach is introduced to offer higher selectivity and outof-band rejection across the whole tuning window. To reduce the loss and to enhance the tuning capabilities, a single tuning circuit in back-to-back configuration is used to control both lower and upper transmission zeros effectively without affecting the frequency passband through controlling the source-load coupling strength between the parallel feeding lines. Measured results show very good agreement with simulations demonstrating distinctive low-loss and high selectivity performance in comparison with similar reported designs.

articleTitle: Design of a mm-Wave Double-Sided Substrate Blass Matrix Beamforming Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work presents a multilayer Blass matrix architecture for mm-Wave applications. Three main problems of the original Blass matrix are tackled with the proposed topology. First, the spurious excitation problem, which is caused by multiple signal paths and degrades the matrix performance, is reduced. Second, our design approach ensures the design of a Blass matrix with the minimum possible losses. Third, directional slot couplers are designed eliminating the crossovers. The proposed design shows a remarkably constant phase difference in the K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> frequency band.

articleTitle: Optimized and Miniaturized Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this work, the performance of Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (CSCMR) systems is studied to achieve optimal Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) efficiency and footprint miniaturization. A traditional CSCMR system from previous work is used to benchmark the performance of the proposed systems. The simulation and measured results demonstrate that by increasing the widths of the Transmitting (TX) and Receiving (RX) resonator loops and reducing source/load loops (while keeping the same overall dimensions) significant miniaturization is achieved. Also, the inner radius of source/load loops is optimized for higher efficiency depending on the resonant frequency of the CSCMR system.

articleTitle: Micro-machined 3D Cube Antenna for X-Band Communication ICs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A 3D cube antenna for CMOS communication ICs is proposed in this paper. The antenna is fabricated on the surface of a cube for the interior CMOS chip placement. The antenna system consists of a meandered line antenna plated gold on three silicon planes of the cube and a balun on one plane. Three planes are then connected and folded by gold, and fixed in a plastic carrier. This antenna is designed for X-band receivers (8-12 GHz) and its measured peak gain is -$1.38\mathrm{d}\mathrm{B}\mathrm{i}$ with 7% -$10\mathrm{d}\mathrm{B}$ reflection coefficient at 10.35 GHz. The antenna cube interior size is 3 $\mathrm{m}\mathrm{m}\times 3\mathrm{m}\mathrm{m}\times 3$ mm, of which the cubic shape allows for CMOS IC packaging inside the cube’s hollow interior.

articleTitle: Analog Predistortion of K-band GaN for 10W Linear Output Power and 30% Power Added Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: As GaN SSPAs begin to supplant TWTAs in space applications, the need for predistortion linearization will follow just as it had been for TWTAs in high data rate communications. This paper reports best-in-class performance for a linearized Kband GaN device. Measurement shows 10W of linear output power and corresponding power added efficiency at 30% when analog predistortion is applied. This is the highest reported efficiency for a packaged K-band GaN device and is achieved with nearly ideal linear performance with <; 0.3dB between Psat and PldB.

articleTitle: Detection of Harmonic Micro-Doppler Signatures Using Passive RF Tags and Harmonic Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: We present a new technique for detecting the motion of objects using a combination of harmonic radar, passive radio-frequency (RF) tags, and micro-motion radar signatures in cluttered environments. A harmonic radar transmitting at 2.5 GHz and receiving at 5 GHz is designed to excite a new passive harmonic tag consisting of two slot-dipole antennas tuned to the two radar bands. The tag receives the 2.5 GHz signal and uses a diode to generate a harmonic response at 5 GHz, which is retransmitted back to the radar. The motion of the tag manifests at the 5 GHz harmonic frequency through the addition of frequency sidebands, called micro-Doppler. We demonstrate the novel harmonic micro-Doppler system, which is able to detect the dynamic motion of harmonic tags in a realistic, cluttered environment. The tag motion is shown using the short time-frequency transform (STFT), demonstrating the ability to detect motion signatures in harmonic radar, and extending earlier works in tacking objects and activities classification.

articleTitle: A Wide Scanning-Angle mmWave AiP Antenna Module for 5G Portable Terminals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Millimeter-Wave (mmW) communication in 5G mobile terminals requires mmW antenna to have low-profile design structure, wide-bandwidth and large-angle beam scanning. In this work, 4×2 array is presented which can be applied for the mmW communications of 5G mobile terminals. The array element design adopts a patch antenna structure with a shorting pin, which can excite an extra zero mode resonant frequency. Combined the 2nd zero mode and the original TM01 mode, the proposed array can give a broadband from 23.5-28 GHz, a large-angle beam scanning with ±60° coverage, as well as a low-profile substrate with 0.508 mm. Then, we designed an antenna in package (AiP) antenna module based on the proposed array, and the measured results have demonstrated good performance.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Small Satellite Optical Communication System based on PathWave System Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Optical communication systems (OCS) are an emerging technology for space applications. OCS have several advantages against traditional RF communication, such as higher transmission rate and unregulated spectrum. With the trend of satellite platform miniaturization, OCS is becoming the prevalent mean for high-data-rate communications for small satellites. This paper presents an overview of existing small satellite OCS showing critical system performance metrics. An OOK (on-off keying) modulation model and simulation of a link between satellites and ground for OCS using performance parameters from recent small satellite missions are presented. The simulations are performed using Keysight PathWave System Design (PSD) and allow for OCS design and study of the effect of key characteristics on the overall system performance.

articleTitle: Domain Decomposition Based Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) Modeling of Acoustic Wave Resonators and Filters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of artificial neural networks (ANNs) as a surrogate modeling method based on machine learning algorithms in emulating the electroacoustic wave behavior of the high-Q piezoelectric resonators and filters. A domain decomposition approach incorporating ANN models to concurrently analyze multidomain radio frequency (RF) modules is also discussed. Different multilayer perceptron (MLP) ANN models have been developed and benchmarked against their model accuracy and model efficiency. The developed models are then utilized to construct ladder-type Band 7 and Band 41 bandpass transmit filters, as examples, to highlight the quality of the modeling method. Other possible applications pertinent to the capability of machine learning algorithms are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Novel Acoustic Wave Networks Comprising Resonators Achieving Prescribed Coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Novel acoustic wave networks comprising resonators achieving prescribed coupling are proposed. The design methodology is based on classic network synthesis of doubly- and/or singly-terminated networks. The synthesis of LTE Band 25 contiguous duplexer prototype is performed and its electrical characteristics are presented.

articleTitle: Building Material Attenuations at 5 GHz and at mmWave Frequencies 30 GHz and 90 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Millimeter wave (mmWave) communication systems will be usedwidely, both indoors and out. Many systems will use directional antennas to overcome attenuation due to free space and obstructions. For specification of link parameters, the attenuation of common materials is of value, and this is the subject of this paper. Measurements were conducted at three frequencies to estimate the attenuation of several common building materials. Frequencies were 5 GHz, and two mmWave frequencies, 30 and 90 GHz. Materials were those found in a typical office building: glass, plasterboard, dropped-ceiling tile, and solid wooden fire doors. We also calculated the attenuation for each material for these frequencies using the commercial ray-tracing tool Wireless InSiteOR, and generally found very good agreement. Most materials exhibit moderate (few dB) attenuation, with the wooden fire doors yielding the largest loss, over 30 dB at 90 GHz. Remarks on the wide range of attenuations on mmWave signals are provided.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging System for Soft Tissue Imaging of Cancer Patients
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In the field of medical imaging, there are many ways to visualize disease pathology in the body. Conventional medical imaging techniques use ionizing radiation, which is harmful to the patient on a cellular level. As more and more imaging tests are being ordered, safer alternatives must be developed to protect the public from these harmful effects. Microwave imaging (MWI) is a novel solution that will produce images while keeping the patient safe from harmful radiation. Lower frequency microwaves are not as harmful to DNA and cellular structures. As a result, a MWI system (MWIS) will be safer for method to acquire medical images. Although this technology has been actively researched for several decades, the proposed design differs in that it will attempt to merge the circular data collection patterns of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging with the reflective nature of radar and ultrasound. Consequently, the proposed system will be able to produce three-dimensional images of the anatomy in a much safer and cheaper manner than conventional imaging methods. As this research is a work in progress, this paper is intended to outline the proposed design as well as current progress of the MWIS.

articleTitle: An S-band Automatically Tunable Bandpass Filter Based on a Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel automatic tuning mechanism that eliminates hand-tuning and is suitable for electronically-tunable microwave filters. The proposed method is based on a machine learning approach using physics-based filter characteristic parameters like resonant frequency, bandwidth, insertion loss, and return loss. The whole tuning process is done automatically and does not require any pre-tuning or human expertise. Furthermore, unlike single-frequency post-production tuning techniques, the presented methodology is applicable to continuously-tunable filters covering a wide frequency range. This method is experimentally tested on an S-band evanescent-mode electronically-tunable bandpass filter that can tune from 2-3. 5GHz. To the best of the author's knowledge, this is the first demonstration of such an automatic tuning mechanism where the user can specify any frequency of interest and the filter tunes automatically to that frequency within the entire operating range of the filter.

articleTitle: Board-Integrated Tunable Bandpass Filter with Wide Stopband for Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this study, a tunable compact substrate integrated cavity based second-order bandpass filter with a wide stopband is presented. The filter is designed to fit within a previously determined phased array antenna stackup. In order to shrink the size of the filter at the fundamental mode, the resonators are capacitively loaded. However, the heavy loading technique brings the resonant frequencies of the higher order modes closer to the fundamental mode of operation. To suppress the closer spurious passband due to the heavy loading, the resonators are designed as stepped-impedance structures. For tuning, varactor diodes are used in series with fixed value high-Q loading capacitors. Effects of different biasing methods on the electromagnetic fields and on the spurious-free range are discussed. To show the validity of our design, the second order filter is fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Channel Emulation for the Characterization of Wearable RFID Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Wearable sensors with RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) tags are considered to be an integral part of the upcoming revolution in the IoT (Internet of Things) sector. As with many deployed IoT sensor systems, dynamic environment conditions present challenges in reliably measuring system performance; this difficulty is enhanced due to proprietary details about the sensors, such as an RFID chip embedded within a novel knitted antenna acting as a passive sensor. A repeatable and scalable platform is necessary to evaluate the performance of the entire system in the pre-deployment stage in order to compare the predicted effects of varying components, design, and integration of sensors in an integrated IoT device. This paper demonstrates the development of an RFID channel emulation testbed in the United States ISM band (902-928 MHz). The testbed includes a commercial RFID interrogator, a custombuilt circuit board housing a commercial passive RFID chip, and a dynamic spectrum environment emulator (DYSE) for wireless channel emulation. A single link scenario was considered where the DYSE emulates the antenna gain fluctuation due to the sensing of breathing with a fabric-based RFID. Two regular and one irregular breathing scenarios were emulated, and breathing rate or anomaly was detected from post-processed RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator) data received by the RFID interrogator.

articleTitle: Radiation Shielding Effectiveness of Additively Manufactured Antenna-on-Package for Space Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: The interest in space exploration by the private sector has been growing rapidly in recent years, along with business models to profit from long-duration space activities. Additive manufacturing in-space (ISM) plays an essential role in long-term space exploration mission sustainability based on on-demand production and recycling of materials. One important issue for electronics in space is their interaction of charged particles which affects the materials' mechanical properties when exposed to the radiation environment of space. This paper reports the effectiveness of radiation shielding 3D-printed ABS and carbon fiber filled nylon composite for short-time exposure. Since carbon fiber filled nylon composite has better shielding effectiveness, a two-layer coupled-fed 3D-printed microstrip antenna is presented for antenna-on-package applications, where the antenna can be used as a radiation shielding element. The fabricated antenna resonates at 5.88 GHz, exhibiting a 10 dB return-loss bandwidth of 5.5 %. A low-cost radiation shielding effectiveness measurement technique is presented, along with the results for ABS and carbon fiber filled nylon composite.

articleTitle: A G-Band Reconfigurable Waveguide-Based Bandstop Filter Enabled by High-Performance Optically Controlled RF Switches
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: We report the design, simulation, and analysis of a G-band (140-220 GHz) reconfigurable bandstop filter (BSF) using the waveguide-based configuration. The reconfigurability is enabled by novel optically controlled RF switches with superior performance in the millimeter-to-terahertz (mmW-THz) region. For a prototype demonstration, multiple such switches are integrated into three pairs of split-ring resonators coupled to a microstrip transmission line for operation. By turning on/off these switches using a 100 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> light from fiber-coupled 550 nm LEDs, the center frequency of the bandstop filter can be reconfigured to 148 GHz, 182 GHz or 212 GHz as expected. For all three states, a center frequency suppression of larger than 15 dB, and an average 3 dB fractional bandwidth of 17.14 % have been achieved. The optically controlled reconfigurable waveguide filter reported here is of unique and high performance, demonstrating the approach for developing tunable/reconfigurable THz circuits using the optically controlled RF switches is promising and transformative for applications in advanced THz sensing, imaging, and adaptive communications.

articleTitle: Toward the Design of a Reconfigurable Liquid-Metal Pixel Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Pixelated liquid-metal (LM) arrays have shown promise in realizing versatile, reconflgurable RF components. However, unused LM pixels introduce parasitic effects. Here we demonstrate comparative designs of a pixelated nodal LM array combining electrocapillary and continuous electrowetting actuation methods. LM is actuated both two dimensionally and three dimensionally to switch between “ON” and “OFF” states. Unused LM elements are hidden at a bottom reservoir during the OFF state, eliminating their parasitic effect.

articleTitle: Tunable S-band Elliptic Bandpass Filter With Constant Absolute Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a tunable bandpass filter in the S band. The proposed design cascades a 5th order elliptic low-pass filter (LPF) and a 5th order elliptical high-pass filter (HPF) to achieve the desired bandpass behavior. The absolute bandwidth of this design is determined by the resonance frequencies (transmission zeros) of the shunt series LC resonators in the elliptic LPF and HPF, respectively. To tune the filter center frequency, the capacitor of each shunt series LC resonator is replaced with a bank of capacitors switched using PIN diodes. To maintain constant absolute bandwidths while tuning center frequency, the transmission zeros of the LPF and HPF branches are tuned simultaneously. At the same time, the impact of finite Q factor of the PIN diodes on filter insertion loss is minimized as a result of tuning the transmission zeros. In addition, the PIN diodes parasitic inductance, at the ON state, is absorbed by the inductance of the shunt series LC resonators. Therefore, wide range tuning can be achieved. The proposed design utilizes three PIN diodes for each shunt branch to achieve a tuning range from 2-3.5GHz with absolute 3dB-bandwidths of ~500MHz. All three tuning states reveal insertion loss better than 2.5dB over the entire tuning range with return loss better than 8dB.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Origami Microwave Absorber
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this work, an ultra-wideband microwave absorber based on a Tachi-Miura Polyhedron (TMP) origami structure is presented. By appropriately folding the TMP at a specific angle, the proposed absorber acts as a honeycomb design, thereby offering superior absorption performance compared to the stateof-the-art absorbers. Specifically, it exhibits an absorptivity of more than 90% in the wide frequency band of 1.22 GHz to 30 GHz for both transverse electric (TE), and transverse magnetic (TM) waves. A fractional bandwidth of 1.84 is supported that proved the ultra-wideband absorption.

articleTitle: Influence of RF Group Delay on the Performance of FMCW Automotive Radar Sensor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this paper, we derive intermediate frequency (IF) level analytical formulation of radio frequency (RF) group delay for automotive frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar waveform under quasi-static approximation. To the best of our knowledge, this paper is the first to develop and simulate an IF-level analytical formulation of RF group delay, including random and deterministic variation for the FMCW radar waveform. Theoretical limitation for the tolerable RF group delay can be derived based on the proposed model. We demonstrated the impact of RF group delay on the FMCW radar sensor's range spectrum in dynamic virtual traffic scenarios. The proposed model is integrated into a virtual FMCW radar sensor model implemented as a functional mock-up unit (FMU) using the standardized interfaces functional mock-up interface (FMI) 2.0 and the open simulation interface (OSI) 3.0.0. A virtual test scenario is implemented in an industry-standard simulation tool, CarMaker, to demonstrate the effect.

articleTitle: Using Standing Waves to Boost RF-DC Sensitivity in PCB Voltage Multiplier Circuit to -15dBm (1.9V DC)
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A novel, 50 Ω, 2-stage voltage multiplier (VM) circuit on PCB with one of the highest RF-DC conversion at 2.4 GHz without an external matching network for ambient RF energy-harvesting is presented in this paper. This circuit has 2 novelties. The first novelty of this design is the use of optimized transmission lines within each stage of the 2 stage voltage multiplier to induce standing wave peaks at the input of the diodes in each stage. Doing so minimizes diode losses and maximizes RF-DC voltage conversion in the voltage multiplier. The 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> novelty is the use of an optimized input feed from the input port to the second stage of the voltage multiplier to cancel out the I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> stage reactance thereby giving a 10dB return loss at 2.4. ADS Simulations of this new PCB based design show a RF-DC sensitivity of-19dBm and- 15dBm for 1V and 1. 9V DC output respectively with a PMU output load of 1 M Ω, which is comparable to CMOS based designs.

articleTitle: A Software Defined Radio Interrogator for Passive Harmonic Transponders
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Passive wireless sensors provide an opportunity for long term monitoring of remote environments. Such devices are activated with an interrogation signal which enables them to transmit information via a return signal. Some systems utilize the same frequency for interrogation and the return, which causes unwanted interference, particularly in cluttered environments. This work considers an interrogation system for a different class of passive devices, i.e., passive harmonic transponders. Specifically, we present the results of a single-board software defined radio (SDR) interrogation system which transmits an interrogation signal at 1.3 GHz and receives a return at 2.6 GHz. The system is demonstrated with a device known as a passive, chipless frequency doubling reflectenna (FDR). The SDR platform enables a compact, low-cost, and quickly operating design. The mean absolute error of the proposed interrogator was found to be 1.15 dB when compared with laboratory instrumentation. Additionally, this system is capable of interrogating at 70 cm with an EIRP of only 0dBm.

articleTitle: 6-to-13 GHz Voltage Controlled Oscillator with 7 dBm Output Power in 22 nm FD-SOI
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) is presented with 6 to 13 GHz tuning range, split into two bands for application in baseband signal processing, multi-leafed or fractional clock-data-recovery architectures. The 22nm FD-SOI is used for the implementation. Cross-coupled p- and the nMOS pairs are used for the oscillator, with the advantages of this circuit detailed. To achieve the high tuning range, inductor switching is implemented. The inductor is custom-designed so a 70% area reduction is obtained in comparison with a standard inductor. This results in an active area for the VCO of 0.02 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. An output butter provides up to 7 dBm output power while the whole circuit supplied at 1V consumes 18mW of which 4.92 mW are drawn by the VCO core. On-wafer measurements show a total tuning range of 70% and phase noise in the low-frequency setting of -96.6dBc/Hz and -85.1dBc/Hz in the high-frequency mode at lMHz offset giving a maximum Figure of merit FOMT of 186.3 dBc. This design stands out for its excellent phase noise, power consumption, area and an outstanding tuning-range for the given operation frequency.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Wireless Power Transfer Systems for Wearable and Implantable Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: The effects of the human body on wearable and implantable Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems, which are based on the Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (CSCMR) method, are studied. Specifically, a CSCMR system's efficiency in free space is compared to its efficiency at several locations on and inside the human body. Simulations were performed using the EM SIM4LIFE software and a detailed human body model (i.e., Duke). The effects of the head, chest, and lower back are examined for wearable applications.

articleTitle: A 60 GHz High Gain Narrow-Band 150 nm InGaAs based Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: The feasibility of inductorless two-stage common-source power amplifier (PA) based on 150nmInGaAs pHEMT devices is evaluated for narrow-band applications at ~60GHz. The PA uses carefully sized and shorted microstrip transmission lines in place of inductors for mm-wave operation. It achieves a maximum gain of 18 dB, an operating 3-dB bandwidth of 2.5 GHz at 62 GHz center frequency with a fractional bandwidth of 4%. The PAE and P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-idB</sub> are 11.8 % and 8.1 dBm, respectively. The area of the layout of the PA is 0.22 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> . The power delivered by the amplifier is 12.8 dBm. The power consumed by the PA is 135 mW at a source voltage of 4 V. A comparison of performance of the proposed PA with alternative technologies shows that it wm be a viable option in 60 GHz circuit design for ultra-short secured wireless links expected to be prevalent in the next decade.

articleTitle: A Broadband, High Dynamic Range DPST Switch and IF Amplifier IC
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work presents a broadband double pole single throw (DPST) switch and an intermediate frequency (IF) amplifier combination integrated circuit (IC) designed for a multiple antenna frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar receiver front-end. The DPST switch and IF amplifier designs feature techniques for enhancing the linearity and bandwidth, whereas on the other hand low noise figure, low DC power consumption and good isolation is maintained. Designed using High Voltage CMOS (HV-CMOS) devices from a 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology, the combined circuit can be operated at supply voltages in range from 3 V-5 V. At the nominal 5 V operation, it delivers a transducer gain of 20 dB, noise Figure of 10 dB, isolation better than 38 dB, whereas the 3 dB gain flatness was measured from 5 MHz to 270 MHz.

articleTitle: Additive Manufactured, On-Package 2.4 GHz Tripolar Antenna System for Cluttered Channels
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A compact, 3D-printed tripolar antenna system operating at 2.4 GHz is presented. The antenna is designed for integration with commercial wireless nodes for the purpose of mitigating channel multipath and depolarization effects that might exist in machine-to-machine environments. The antenna is fabricated as a single piece, utilizing fused deposition modeling for dielectric parts and micro-dispensing of silver paste for conductive layers. Over the air testing demonstrates that by leveraging the diversity provided by the three mutually orthogonal monopoles, a 1% channel improvement of 11 dB can be achieved in a highly reflective, fading environment. This improvement leads to better bit error rate (BER) performance. Additionally, RSSI measurements show significant improvement when the prototype antenna system is integrated with a commercially available wireless sensor.

articleTitle: Estimation of Background Medium’s Properties in Microwave Holographic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this paper, an approach is proposed to enhance the images produced by holographic microwave imaging technique. The approach estimates the electrical properties of the background medium. For that, first, we assumed that the background properties are within a pre-known range. Then, wideband holographic imaging technique is applied to two sets of frequencies to reconstruct two sets of images for assumed property values within the pre-determined range. An error is computed to record the differences between the two sets of images. The error is expected to be minimum at the true values of the background medium's properties. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the validity of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: A Physically Reconfigurable 1× 8 Monolithic Thick Origami Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a 1×8 monolithic thick origami antenna array. The proposed design dynamically adjusts its radiation pattern through foldability, without the need of any additional phase shifters in its feeding network. Depending on its folded state, the array can cover different regions in space by switching from a single beam at broadside, to two beams at θ = ±45°, and four beams at θ = ±45°, ±135°. The foldability of the design is implemented using three lamina emergent torsional joint surrogate hinges. These hinges allow the array to physically reconfigure to different folded states and pack itself efficiently to an area that is four times smaller than its deployed area. For demonstration purposes our proposed array is designed to operate at 2.45 GHz using a single 1.55 mm thick FR4 substrate.

articleTitle: Collaborative Edge Processing by mmWave Access Providing UAVs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A wireless IoT system consisting of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is investigated. They work with a ground base station to provide mmWave access to user equipment and IoT devices. In parallel, they collaboratively share edge processing load. We design a modified Lyapunov optimization framework for assigning tasks to multi-hop connected UAVs. The proposed strategy constructs a task flow control policy that is near-optimal with respect to energy consumption and response time. The best task migration and distribution over the UAVs can be found out at a bearable complexity. Numerical results confirm the soundness of the framework regarding power cost, execution latency and overhead data.

articleTitle: Dual-Band 2:1 LC-tank Injection-Locked Frequency Divider Using Distributed Transformer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this article, a wide locking dual-band 2:1 LCresonator injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD) designed in the tsmc 0.18 μm BiCMOS process is presented. The 2:1 ILFD uses two sub-ILFDs with a concentric transformer. The low-band ILFD uses an outer 5-turn octagonal center-tapped inductor and the parasitic capacitors to build the primary LC-resonator. The high-band ILFD uses an inner 3-turn octagonal center-tapped inductor and the parasitic capacitors to build the secondary LC-resonator. Varactors are added to the strips of inductors to emulate the parasitic capacitor. The resonator is a distributed transformer resonator. While tuning the varactors two frequency tuning ranges are measured. At the supply voltage of 0.75 V, the core power consumption is 2.87 mW. The low-band locking range at P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">inj</sub> = 0 dBm is 5.5 GHz (129.4%) from 1.5 GHz to 7 G. The high-band locking range at P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">inj</sub> = 0 dBm is 3.6 GHz (27.69%) from 11.2 GHz to 14.8 GFlz. The die occupies an area of 0.933 × 0.993 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: 5G enabled Mobile Operating Hospital and Emergency Care Service
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Critical care has frequently been fatal for trauma patients suffering from hemorrhage. The pre-hospital communication gap between the paramedics and the doctors contributes most towards this. This paper discusses a system model of a 5G-enabled communication architecture among the major trauma centres in the Greater Manchester. An Internet of sensors acquires and wirelessly communicates biosignals from the patient in real time, using 5G. These signals are then displayed as parameters to the closest trauma care management centres. This paper proposes a connectivity model that supports such a system by assessing and identifying the most optimal path for signal transmittance. A system-level 5G network modelling and simulation findings reveal that a signal-to-noise ratio of over 2dB is achieved for two base stations between the incident site and the nearest emergency medical centre. This value decreases by over 5 dB as the number of base station doubles. Hence, reconfigurable 5G base stations connectivity subsystems are required for critical vertical use cases of the radio standard.

articleTitle: On the bending effects of a printed 4x4 antenna array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 21st Annual Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: The bending effects of proximity coupled 4×4 patch arrays with printed patch elements operating in the X-band near 10 GHz is presented. The patch arrays have circular patch elements with inclusive slots residing on the top surface of four layers (10 mil/layer) of DuPont Pyralux AP. The inclusive slots decrease the axial ratio of the antenna and increase the impedance bandwidth. Each array has a microstrip feed network of quarterwave transformers and T-junction power dividers in the middle of the four layer stackup. The microstrip lines are proximity (or capacitively) coupled to the patch elements. A ground plane on the bottom surface of the four layer stackup provides surface agnostic behavior. The patch elements and microstrip feed network are printed with DuPont CB028 conductive ink using a liquid dispense technique. For the purpose of comparison to PCB processed antennas, 4×4 patch arrays with 1/2 oz. electroplated copper for the patch elements and microstrip feed network are also reported. The gain, 3 dB beamwidth, and VSWR bandwidth behavior have been studied for uniaxial bending of the two arrays for radii of curvature down to a 1 inch. The nominal (i.e., no bending) measured far-field gain of the arrays is 14.5 dBi (printed) and 14.7 dBi (copper). The printed and copper arrays behave very similarly with changes in gain of 9.3 dB (printed) and 8.3 dB (copper) for bending down to 1 inch in an axial direction and changes in gain of 2.6 dB (printed) and 2.8 dB (copper) for bending down to 1 inch in a circumferential direction.
